question: Open the Yell listing, click through to all 34 reviews, and copy the sharpest sentence out of each one — word for word, exactly as it is written, punctuation and all.
why: The reviews are the entire site. Every excerpt has to be verbatim and no machine can read Yell, so this is a person with the listing open and a keyboard. Until it is done the review fields render as dated, linked frames with no words in them — honest, but half a site.
where: content/reviews.ts → the `excerpt` field on each review. Read REVIEWS.md first, it is written for a non-developer.

question: Which towns do you actually go to? Flint obviously — but Deeside? Connah's Quay? Holywell? Mold? Buckley? Chester? Where do you stop?
why: The area field and the page titles are built from this list, and it is the single biggest thing that decides whether he turns up in local searches. Towns he does not cover must not be named — that is spam, and it also means driving somewhere he did not want to go.
where: content/areas.ts → add each town with confirmed: true

question: Read me your mobile number digit by digit. Is 07928 784903 right, and is it the number you want ringing?
why: It is on every screen of the site and it is the only way anyone contacts him. The label and the tap-to-call link come from one constant, so it is either right everywhere or wrong everywhere. Dial it before launch.
where: content/site.ts → PHONE_E164, then set PHONE_CONFIRMED = true

question: Is your public liability insurance current, and when does it renew? Same for the CSCS card — is it in date, and what does it say on it?
why: Both are on his Yell listing, which is of unknown vintage. A lapsed insurance claim printed on a website is worse than saying nothing at all. Nothing is printed until each one is confirmed current.
where: content/site.ts → credentials[], set confirmed: true on the ones that check out

question: What hours do you actually work, and when is it fine to ring you? Yell says you are open 24 hours a day, seven days a week — that cannot be right.
why: "Open 24 Hours" is a directory default, not a fact, and an aggregator carries different hours again. The hours section is omitted entirely rather than ship something untrue.

question: Have you got a Google Business Profile — the thing that puts you on the map when someone searches? Can you get into it? What is the link?
why: For a Flint decorator the Google profile will out-earn the website on its own, and it is free. The site links to it and it links back. It also gives /leave-a-review somewhere to send people other than Yell.
where: content/site.ts → googleProfileUrl and googleReviewUrl. If he has not got one, LAUNCH.md step 2 sets it up.

question: Is this your Yell listing? yell.com/biz/a-edwards-decorating-flint-7648594 — and have you ever claimed it, or does it still say "is this your business?"
why: Every review on the site links to it and the schema points at it. It was found by search, not verified, because Yell blocks automated access. One click confirms it. Claiming it is free and lets him add the website address.
where: content/site.ts → yellListingUrl, then set yellListingConfirmed = true

question: Open the listing and read out the rating and the number of reviews at the top of it.
why: 4.9 from 34 is printed in type on the front of the site with its source and date. It came into the build second-hand. Someone has to have looked at it.
where: content/reviews.ts → yellRating, then set seenOnListing: true

question: aedwardsdecorating.co.uk is free — shall I register it? It is about a tenner a year.
why: There is no domain, no website and nothing to put on the Yell listing or the van. Checked and available on 11 August 2026, along with the .com and .uk.
where: content/site.ts → set DOMAIN_REGISTERED = true and NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL in the host's environment

question: Can you send me the photos off your phone — the originals, straight out of the camera roll, not off Yell? Say which room and which village each one is.
why: The photo strip is the one field on the site with pictures in it, and it only appears if the originals turn up. The copies on Yell are compressed and belong to Yell. If nothing comes, the field stays cut and the site is fine.

question: Have you got an email address you actually check? If not, do you want one setting up on the new domain?
why: The enquiry form has nowhere to deliver to without one, so it is hidden and the page shows the phone number instead. An invented address that bounces is worse than no form.
where: content/site.ts → email, and ENQUIRY_TO in the host's environment

question: Once the site is live, can we add the web address to your Yell listing? It is a free field.
why: The listing is the only thing sending him work at the moment. Pointing it at the site is the cheapest link he will ever get.

question: n/a — a job for whoever has the listing open.
why: Each review currently links to the listing rather than to itself, because Yell's per-review link format could not be checked. If the listing gives each review its own anchor, use it — one tap to the exact review is more convincing than one tap to a page of them.

question: How long have you been decorating? Not how long you have been on Yell — how long altogether.
why: The site currently says only what it can prove: over ten years on Yell. If he has been at it for twenty-five, that is worth a line. It is not worth a guess.
